title: Parent discloses excessive identity data during registration
description: The parent sends highly sensitive personal data to register, including government ID alongside email, name, password, and a six-digit code. If full government ID is not strictly necessary at registration, the act of sharing creates a disclosure risk because more personal data than needed leaves the parent.
assumptions: Assumes government ID collection at initial registration may exceed strict necessity for account creation or age/guardian verification.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort because the retrieved context gives applicability by threat type but not detailed node taxonomy.

title: Registration payload can identify the parent in transit
description: The data flow contains direct identifiers and highly identifying attributes such as email, name, and government ID. If the transmission is observable, intercepted, or insufficiently protected, the payload can directly identify the parent.
uncertainty_note: Assumes transport-layer or intermediary exposure is plausible; if strong end-to-end transport protection is enforced, likelihood would be lower. Tree-node id is approximate.

title: Registration transmission enables linkage of the parent across contexts
description: Combining email, name, government ID, and registration metadata on this flow can allow records about the same parent to be linked across systems or sessions. Even if some fields are pseudonymous elsewhere, this flow carries enough information to correlate identities.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; linkage may depend on observer access to other datasets.

title: Sensitive registration data may be disclosed in transit
description: This flow carries password, government ID, and other personal data. If the channel, intermediaries, logs, or monitoring infrastructure expose the payload or metadata, confidential registration information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Assumes possible exposure in transit or via network/security tooling; likelihood depends strongly on deployment controls. Tree-node id is approximate.

title: Authentication service may over-collect or retain sensitive registration data
description: On receipt, the authentication service processes and may store email, name, government ID, password-derived data, and the six-digit code. If it stores raw government ID, retains the code unnecessarily, or uses the data beyond registration/authentication purposes, this creates a disclosure risk at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the service may persist or further process the received attributes rather than immediately minimizing them.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; exact applicability depends on storage and retention design.

title: Authentication service may process registration data without sufficient transparency or valid basis
description: The destination receives highly sensitive personal data, including government ID. If the service lacks clear notice, purpose specification, lawful basis/consent where required, or an option to avoid unnecessary fields, the collection and processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy/legal obligations require transparency, purpose limitation, and data minimization for this registration flow.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and actual notices/controls; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Authentication service can infer additional sensitive attributes from registration data
description: Government ID and identity details may allow the service to infer nationality, age, sex, region, or other attributes beyond what the parent explicitly intended to provide for authentication. This creates an unawareness risk if such inferences are not expected or explained.
assumptions: Assumes the government ID format or associated verification processes reveal additional attributes.
uncertainty_note: Inference potential depends on the specific government ID scheme and service behavior; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or contest what registration data was submitted
description: If the authentication service does not provide adequate confirmation, receipts, or auditable records of the submitted registration details and consent/notice state, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate what was actually provided or dispute inaccurate records.
assumptions: Assumes lack of user-visible confirmation or auditability for submitted registration data.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible but lower-confidence threat because the flow description does not specify audit/receipt mechanisms; tree-node id is approximate.

title: Excessive storage of parent account personal data
description: The users collection may store more parent-account personal data than is strictly necessary for authentication/account management. Persisting unnecessary attributes increases avoidable disclosure risk because the data becomes available to anyone or any component with access to the datastore.
assumptions: Assumes 'store parent account' includes personal data beyond a minimal identifier/credential record, such as profile, contact, or child-related account context.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; the exact subnode may vary with the project's threat-tree version.

title: Parent account records may be linkable across contexts
description: If the stored parent account uses stable identifiers such as email address, phone number, username, customer ID, or shared household identifiers, records in the users collection can be linked with other datasets or internal contexts, enabling correlation of the same parent across services or activities.
assumptions: Assumes the stored account contains persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers reused elsewhere.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ by version; applicability depends on whether stable identifiers are stored.

title: Stored parent account data may enable identification
description: Data written to the users collection may directly identify a parent (for example by name, email, phone number, or unique account identifier) or indirectly identify them when combined with other stored attributes.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account contains direct identifiers or a combination of attributes sufficient to single out a person.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent if the account record contains direct identifiers; if only pseudonymous identifiers are stored, likelihood/severity may be lower.

title: Parent account data may be stored or reused beyond user expectations
description: A parent may not expect all submitted account information to be retained in the users collection indefinitely or reused for purposes beyond authentication, such as analytics, profiling, support, or cross-service account correlation. This creates an unawareness risk if storage scope, retention, or downstream uses are not transparent.
assumptions: Assumes notices/UX do not fully explain what account data is stored, for how long, and for which purposes.
uncertainty_note: This depends strongly on the surrounding notice/consent design, which is not provided.

title: Storing parent account data without an appropriate legal basis or valid consent
description: If the users collection stores parent account personal data without a valid legal basis, or if consent/parental authorization is not properly obtained where required, the storage operation may be non-compliant with applicable privacy regulation and purpose-limitation requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes personal data subject to privacy law and that legal basis/consent management may be incomplete or mismatched to the stored fields/purposes.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and the exact nature of the parent-account data and service.

title: Excessive disclosure of user data to parent
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the returned user data contains more attributes than are necessary for the parent-facing purpose, the source process causes unnecessary disclosure of the authenticated user's personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the payload includes personal attributes beyond the minimum needed for the parent to complete the session or task.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement at a high level because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Identity disclosure via JWT or accompanying user data in transit
description: The JWT and accompanying user data may directly identify the authenticated user, or reveal stable identifiers that allow identification if the flow is observed in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the token or payload contains identifiers, claims, or personal data and that transport protections may be insufficient or endpoints/logging expose the content.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transport confidentiality or endpoint/network visibility is not fully controlled; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Linkability through stable identifiers in JWT claims
description: A JWT commonly carries stable claims such as subject identifiers, tenant identifiers, session identifiers, or role information. These can enable linking multiple interactions or sessions belonging to the same user across requests or services if reused or observable.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers are present in the token or metadata and are reused across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Exact claims are not provided, so applicability depends on token design.

title: Further disclosure by parent recipient after receipt
description: Once the parent user receives the JWT and user data, the recipient may store, forward, screenshot, or otherwise share the data beyond the intended authentication purpose, causing additional disclosure at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the external entity can retain or redistribute the received data.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side privacy risk for data delivered to an external entity, but the exact downstream behavior is unknown.

title: Lack of transparency or control over recipient-side retention and use
description: After receiving the JWT and user data, the parent user may not be constrained by system-enforced privacy controls regarding retention, reuse, or onward sharing. This can undermine the data subject's awareness and control over how their data is handled after delivery.
assumptions: Assumes limited technical or policy controls once data reaches the external entity.
uncertainty_note: Mapped as non-compliance / policy-control risk based on limited context; exact legal or policy obligations are not specified.

title: Credentials and parent email can identify the child account if intercepted in transit
description: The login flow carries a parent email address and password. The email address is directly identifying for the family/account, and even traffic metadata around repeated login attempts may help identify a specific child account or household if the flow is observable in transit.
assumptions: Applies if transport confidentiality is weak, absent, or terminates in an untrusted intermediary; metadata visibility may remain even with encrypted payloads.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context only gave applicable threat types/positions, not detailed node ids.

title: Disclosure of parent email and password during transmission
description: The flow contains highly sensitive authentication data. If the data flow is intercepted, logged by intermediaries, or sent over an inadequately protected channel, the parent email and password could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes possible network eavesdropping, TLS misconfiguration, interception by proxies, or accidental logging of request contents in transit.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Authentication service may disclose submitted credentials or account data through logging or improper handling
description: On receipt of the login request, the authentication service could expose the parent email or even password through verbose application logs, monitoring tools, debugging traces, crash reports, or onward sharing beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the service or its operational tooling may retain or expose raw request fields.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-judgement due to limited retrieved node-level context.

title: Authentication service may process parent credentials beyond the child's reasonable expectations
description: A child login using a parent email and password creates a risk that the authentication service uses these credentials for secondary purposes, such as analytics, profiling, cross-service correlation, or retention beyond what is needed to authenticate the session.
assumptions: Assumes purposes, retention, or downstream uses are broader than strictly necessary for login.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on actual backend practices; included because the destination's receipt and processing of parent credentials creates a plausible unawareness risk.

title: Child may not have meaningful choice or age-appropriate consent regarding use of parent credentials
description: Because the login flow requires a parent email and password, the child may not understand how the parent's credentials and associated personal data are processed, and the service may lack mechanisms to ensure appropriate parental authorization, transparency, or age-appropriate consent handling.
assumptions: Relevant where the service targets or knowingly serves children and relies on parent credentials as part of access.
uncertainty_note: This is a contextual compliance threat; exact applicability depends on jurisdiction, age-gating, and parental authorization design.

title: Authentication service can link child activity to the parent's identity across sessions
description: Using a parent email as the login identifier enables the destination process to correlate repeated child logins and potentially link the child's account, device, or behavior with the parent's identity and other family accounts or services.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is stable and reused across sessions or services.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is approximate; the linkage risk itself is strong for this flow.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile data to the child user
description: The authentication service returns not only a JWT but also child profiles. If the profiles contain more attributes than are necessary for immediate authentication/session establishment, the source process discloses personal data beyond the minimum needed on this flow.
assumptions: Assumes 'child profiles' may include profile attributes not strictly required at login or token issuance.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: JWT and profile payload can enable linkability across sessions or services if observed in transit
description: A JWT carrying a stable subject identifier and userType=child, together with profile data, can act as a persistent correlator. If the flow is observable or logged by intermediaries, the token claims or associated metadata may allow linking multiple interactions to the same child.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifiers or claims reused across requests, or that transport/intermediary logs expose correlatable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies primarily if transport confidentiality, token minimization, or logging controls are weak.

title: JWT claims and profile data may identify the child if exposed in transit
description: The flow explicitly contains userType=child and child profiles. If intercepted, decoded from an unprotected token, or exposed via logs/URLs, these data may directly or indirectly identify the child.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is readable by parties beyond the intended recipient or that metadata/logging exposes identifying claims.
uncertainty_note: If the JWT is opaque to observers and transport/logging are well protected, likelihood is lower.

title: Data disclosure of child account information in transit
description: This flow carries authentication material and child profile information. Without strong transport protection and careful handling of caches/logs, confidential child data could be disclosed during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Generic but genuine for this flow because it contains child-related personal data and authentication artifacts.

title: Insufficient transparency to the child about profile data delivered at login
description: The child user may receive a JWT and profile data without clear notice about what profile attributes are included, why they are provided at authentication time, how long they remain valid, or how they will be used by the client/application.
assumptions: Assumes the receiving interface does not clearly explain the contents and purpose of the returned profile data/token.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side unawareness threat framed around the recipient's lack of visibility; applicability depends on the UX and notices shown.

title: Potential non-compliance from sending child profile data without strict necessity or appropriate child-data safeguards
description: Because the flow concerns a child user, returning profile data together with authentication may violate data-minimization or child-specific privacy obligations if not strictly necessary, properly justified, and protected.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child-privacy/data-protection requirements and that some returned profile fields may be unnecessary for authentication.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations are jurisdiction- and context-dependent; exact legal basis is not provided.

title: Excessive disclosure by parent during child-profile creation
description: The parent user may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary when creating the child profile, especially given the sensitivity of the attributes involved (name, date of birth, gender, government ID). The act of sharing this full set of attributes creates a privacy risk if all fields are not required for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes some of the requested attributes may be optional or not strictly necessary for initial profile creation.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on generic disclosure-at-source reasoning; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree citation may differ.

title: Identification of the child in transit from direct identifiers and quasi-identifiers
description: The data flow contains strong identifiers and quasi-identifiers — notably name, date of birth, gender, and government ID — that can directly identify the child or make the child readily identifiable if intercepted, logged, or otherwise exposed in transit.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; applicability of identifiability on this flow is high given the attribute set.

title: Linkability of child records via recurring identifiers and attribute combination
description: The combination of name, date of birth, gender, and especially government ID enables this profile-creation event to be linked with other records about the same child across sessions, systems, or datasets. Even metadata about the parent-to-profile-management interaction could contribute to linking.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; the threat clearly applies because the flow includes a persistent identifier and strong quasi-identifiers.

title: Over-collection and retention of sensitive child attributes by Child Profile Management
description: Upon receipt, Child Profile Management may collect, store, or further process more child data than necessary for profile creation, particularly the government ID and full demographic details. This creates a disclosure risk at the destination if the process retains or uses the data beyond the minimum needed purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the destination stores or processes the received attributes and that necessity/minimization controls are not yet established.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; threat is grounded in destination-side unnecessary disclosure/over-collection.

title: Unawareness about downstream use of child identity data
description: The receiving process may use the child's personal data for purposes, retention periods, verification steps, or sharing practices that are not transparent to the parent at the time of profile creation. This creates a privacy threat if the parent is not adequately informed about how the child's data will be handled.
assumptions: Assumes notice/transparency around processing purposes, retention, and sharing may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; included because profile creation commonly involves opaque downstream processing unless explicitly documented.

title: Non-compliance risk from collecting child government ID and demographic data
description: Collecting and processing a child's government ID together with other personal attributes may trigger heightened legal and policy obligations, including data minimization, purpose limitation, child-data protections, and potentially parental-consent requirements. If Child Profile Management lacks an adequate legal basis or collects more than necessary, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy/data-protection obligations for children's data and sensitive identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate and jurisdiction-dependent, but the compliance risk is genuine given child data and government ID.

title: Excessive child-profile data written to storage
description: When Child Profile Management stores or updates a child profile, it may send more personal data than is strictly necessary for the intended purpose. This creates avoidable disclosure because sensitive child data becomes persisted in the datastore even if some attributes are not required for profile management.
assumptions: Assumes child profiles contain personal data about minors and that some fields may be optional or not strictly necessary for the storage purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ in the full threat tree.

title: Over-retention of child-profile data in the database
description: Upon receipt of stored or updated child-profile data, the childprofiles collection may retain historical or current profile data longer than necessary, including outdated or superseded values from updates. This results in avoidable disclosure because personal data about children remains available in storage beyond the justified retention period.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore or surrounding persistence logic keeps records, versions, backups, or undeleted fields after updates.
uncertainty_note: Exact retention behavior is not stated in the flow description; included because store/update operations commonly create privacy risk through unnecessary persistence.

title: Child-profile records may be stored without sufficient user awareness
description: Storing or updating a child profile in the database may occur without the data subject or guardian being adequately informed that the profile data is persisted, what fields are stored, and for what purposes. This undermines transparency and intervenability regarding the storage operation.
assumptions: Assumes notice about persistence details may be incomplete or not presented at the time profile data is managed.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on the surrounding UX and privacy notice, which are not shown in the DFD; tree-node id is best judgement.

title: Child-profile storage may lack a valid legal basis or guardian consent
description: Persisting or updating child profile data in the datastore may occur without an appropriate legal basis, or without obtaining and recording any required parental/guardian consent for processing children's personal data. This creates a non-compliance risk tied directly to the storage operation.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes personal data of children and may be subject to child-specific consent or lawful-basis requirements.
uncertainty_note: Applicable legal obligations depend on jurisdiction and the nature of the child-profile data; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Profile-update traffic can link repeated writes to the same child record
description: Metadata on this flow, such as stable record identifiers, account identifiers, or repeated update patterns, can allow observers or intermediaries with access to the transmission context to link multiple store/update events to the same child profile. Even if payload contents are protected, the flow metadata may support correlation over time.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries stable identifiers or otherwise observable metadata associated with a child profile update.
uncertainty_note: This is a generic in-transit metadata linkage risk; actual exposure depends on deployment architecture and transport protections.

title: Database storage enables linkage of child-profile data across updates and datasets
description: Once stored in the childprofiles collection, profile records can be linked across multiple updates and potentially with other collections using persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers. This can create richer longitudinal profiles of a child than necessary for the immediate purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 stores stable identifiers or attributes that permit correlation across records or systems.
uncertainty_note: Exact linkage mechanisms are not described; threat is inferred from persistent profile storage.

title: Stored child-profile attributes may enable identification of a child
description: The childprofiles collection may store direct identifiers or combinations of attributes that make a child identifiable, even if identification was not strictly necessary for every processing purpose. Persisting identifiable child data increases privacy risk because the database becomes a point where identity can be resolved.
assumptions: Assumes child profiles include direct identifiers or sufficiently unique combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifying fields are not listed in the flow description; threat is inferred from the notion of a child profile.

title: Child user directly identifies themselves in search queries or comments
description: The child may submit search terms, requests, likes, or especially comments containing their real name, contact details, school, location, or other identifiers. The act of sending this content to the service can reveal the child's identity.
assumptions: Free-text inputs such as search and comment fields are available and not fully constrained.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort based on general LINDDUN identification threats; exact subnode may vary.

title: Search, like, and comment actions disclose sensitive interests or opinions
description: The child's interactions with videos can reveal personal interests, beliefs, emotional state, or other sensitive traits. Even if the child is not explicitly named, the content of requests and interactions may disclose personal information.
assumptions: Video topics may include sensitive categories, and interaction content is associated with the child account or session.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subnode may differ depending on the threat-tree granularity used.

title: Interaction metadata can link the child's actions across sessions or contexts
description: The flow carries repeated behavioral events such as searches, requests, likes, and comments. Metadata and persistent identifiers in transit, such as account IDs, device IDs, session tokens, IP address, or timing patterns, can enable linking multiple actions to the same child over time.
assumptions: Requests include stable or quasi-stable identifiers or observable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability at the data-flow level.

title: Identifiers in transit can identify the child user
description: If the flow includes account identifiers, usernames, cookies, device identifiers, or network metadata, the child may be identifiable from the transmitted data even when the payload is limited to interaction events.
assumptions: The service uses authenticated or pseudonymous sessions and transmits related identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Applies especially where transport metadata or application identifiers are available.

title: Video service can build a linked profile of the child's behavior
description: On receipt of searches, requests, likes, and comments, the service can correlate these events into a persistent profile of the child, linking behavior across time, topics, and devices.
assumptions: P2 stores or analyzes interaction history per account, device, or session.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact linkability subnode may vary.

title: Received interactions disclose the child's preferences and potentially sensitive traits
description: The destination process can infer preferences, habits, vulnerabilities, and potentially special-category information from the child's searches, viewing requests, likes, and comments.
assumptions: P2 logs and analyzes interaction content and history.
uncertainty_note: General disclosure threat; exact subnode may differ.

title: Child may not understand how interaction data will be used
description: The service may process the child's searches, likes, comments, and requests for personalization, moderation, analytics, or profiling in ways that are not transparent or understandable to a child user, undermining uninformed consent or awareness.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations are absent, complex, or not child-friendly.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to unawareness; exact node may vary.

title: Processing child interaction data may violate child-privacy obligations
description: Collecting and using a child's search, request, like, and comment data may trigger heightened legal obligations, such as parental consent, data minimization, age-appropriate transparency, retention limits, and restrictions on profiling or behavioral advertising. Failure to manage this properly creates a non-compliance threat.
assumptions: The user is a child and the service is subject to child-specific privacy or data-protection requirements.

title: Service may be unable to prove valid consent or user authorization for child interactions
description: If the service relies on consent or parental authorization for collecting and processing the child's interaction data, inadequate records or provenance for these requests and actions can create repudiation-related privacy risk.
assumptions: Processing depends on consent, parental authorization, or demonstrable user action records.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability depends on whether consent/authorization evidence is in scope for this flow.

title: Storage of more video metadata or file content than necessary
description: The Video Management Service may write video files and associated metadata to persistent storage even when some fields or content are not strictly necessary for the stated purpose. This creates avoidable disclosure through collection and storage of personal data beyond data-minimization needs.
assumptions: Video metadata and files can contain personal data such as uploader identifiers, timestamps, location, device details, faces, voices, or other identifying content.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-judgement minimization/storage disclosure node; exact sub-node citation may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Persistent disclosure risk from storing identifiable video metadata and files
description: Once received by the datastore, the stored video metadata and file content may expose personal data to anyone with logical or physical access to the collection. Centralized persistence increases the impact of any later access, backup exposure, replication, or secondary use.
assumptions: MongoDB collection contents are retained and may be accessible to administrators, backup systems, replicas, or downstream consumers.
uncertainty_note: Framed as a destination-side disclosure risk caused by receipt and storage; exact tree-node granularity is approximate.

title: Identified information present in video metadata during transfer
description: The flow may carry metadata containing directly identifying information, such as account identifiers, filenames, uploader references, device identifiers, or other labels tied to a person. Even if the video payload is protected, the metadata itself can identify individuals.
assumptions: This flow includes metadata alongside or about the video files.

title: Video metadata enables linking of records across uploads or services
description: The Video Management Service may include stable identifiers in stored metadata, allowing multiple videos or related records to be linked to the same individual, device, account, or session. This can enable profiling across uploads and over time.
assumptions: Metadata includes persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers such as user IDs, device IDs, IP-related data, or consistent filenames.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node for linking is not available in retrieved context; node citation is best judgement.

title: Stored video metadata and content may allow inference of sensitive attributes
description: By storing video files together with metadata, the datastore enables later analysis that can infer habits, relationships, location patterns, biometric traits, or other sensitive information beyond the original apparent purpose of storage.
assumptions: Video content and metadata are rich enough to support inference, alone or when combined with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability/disclosure distinction can vary depending on model scope; classified here as data-derived inference/discoverability risk using best judgement.

title: Secondary use of stored videos or metadata beyond user expectations
description: After storage in the collection, video files and metadata may be reused for analytics, moderation training, recommendation, or operational debugging in ways users did not expect or were not clearly informed about.
assumptions: The datastore supports later reuse by internal services or operators beyond the immediate upload/retrieval purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node citation is approximate; threat applicability depends on actual governance and notice provided.

title: Retention of video data may exceed consented or declared purposes
description: Persisting video files and metadata in the datastore may conflict with user consent choices or declared retention limits if the collection keeps data longer, in broader scope, or for more purposes than agreed.
assumptions: Consent, notice, or policy constraints exist regarding storage duration, scope, or purpose.
uncertainty_note: Applicable when consent or policy constraints govern this data; exact node citation is best judgement.

title: Excessive collection and storage of child behavioral history
description: The Child Profile Management process stores child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection. Search and watch history are highly revealing behavioral data about a child; storing more detail, duration, or retention than strictly necessary creates an avoidable disclosure of personal data to the system.
assumptions: Assumes the full or granular search/watch history is persisted rather than only minimal aggregates strictly needed for the service.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best-fit LINDDUN Pro judgment for unnecessary/excessive disclosure via collection/storage; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Stored child history enables linkage across sessions and activities
description: By storing search and watch history in a persistent child profile record, the datastore can enable linking multiple viewing/search events over time to the same child profile. This may allow construction of a longitudinal behavioral profile beyond what is necessary for the immediate transaction.
assumptions: Assumes records are keyed by a stable child/profile identifier and retained over time.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ; threat is the linkability created by persistent storage of behavioral events.

title: Child profile history may identify a child through unique interests or combinations of events
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, a stored combination of search terms, watched content, timestamps, and profile references can make a child identifiable within the system or to authorized insiders, especially when interests or viewing patterns are distinctive.
assumptions: Assumes history entries include timestamps, content identifiers, queries, or profile references that together can single out a child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node selection; identifiability may depend on the granularity of stored history.

title: Stored history allows inference of sensitive traits about the child
description: Search and watch history can reveal or support inference of sensitive information such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, ethnicity, developmental issues, or other intimate traits. Persisting this history in the datastore creates a detectability threat because observers or internal actors can detect the child's interests or conditions from the stored records.
assumptions: Assumes the history contains sufficiently descriptive queries/content metadata to support such inferences.
uncertainty_note: Detectability vs disclosure boundaries can vary by interpretation; this entry focuses on the ability to detect sensitive traits from stored history.

title: Secondary use of child history beyond the child's or guardian's expectations
description: Once stored in the childprofiles collection, search and watch history may be reused for personalization, analytics, experimentation, moderation, or marketing-related purposes that are not transparent to the child or guardian. Such downstream use can exceed the original expected purpose of providing the immediate service.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation and user/guardian expectations are not strictly enforced for this stored history.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may vary; the core issue is use of stored behavioral history for purposes beyond the expected one.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for storing child search and watch history
description: Storing a child's search and watch history in the profile datastore may occur without clear notice, meaningful parental authorization where required, or an easy way to review/delete the data. This creates a non-compliance risk with transparency, consent/authorization, and children's data protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the system may be subject to child-specific privacy obligations and that notice/consent/rights handling is not fully implemented.
uncertainty_note: Legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and product context; node id is best-fit for transparency/consent non-compliance.

title: Excessive disclosure in uploaded video content
description: The parent may upload videos that reveal more personal data than necessary for the stated purpose (e.g., child identity, home interior, location cues, other family members). The act of sharing the raw video with the service creates a disclosure risk.
assumptions: Uploaded videos can contain rich visual/audio personal data beyond what is strictly needed for moderation or approval.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context did not include the detailed D threat tree.

title: Linkability via upload metadata and network identifiers
description: The upload flow may expose stable identifiers or metadata such as account identifiers, device identifiers, IP address, timestamps, file hashes, or repeated content characteristics that allow linking this upload to the same parent across sessions or services.
assumptions: Transport or application-layer metadata is available to the receiving service or intermediaries and can be correlated over time.
